question: Which of the following was NOT built by Shah Jahan?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Buland Darwaza**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Buland Darwaza**:

 
 
• This grand gateway was built by **Akbar** in 1576 as part of the **Fatehpur Sikri** complex to commemorate his victory over Gujarat.
 
• It is one of the highest gateways in the world and reflects Akbar's architectural style.
 
• So it is not built by Shah Jahan
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Shalimar Gardens**:

 
 
• These gardens were commissioned by **Shah Jahan** in **1630** in Lahore (now in Pakistan).
 
• The Shalimar Garden is one of the finest examples of Mughal garden design,** also known as "Charbagh"** (four-part garden).
 
 
 
• **Red Fort (Delhi)**:
 
 
• It is situated on the Banks of River Yamuna.
 
• The fort was designated a UNESCO World Heritage site in 2007. 
 
• Indo-Islamic and Mughal architectural styles are present in the Red Fort Complex.
 
• Ustad Ahmad Lahauri was the architect of the Red Fort.
 
• Red Fort is the fusion of the Timurids and the Persians architectural styles. 
 
• Shah Jahan commissioned construction of the Red Fort on 12 May 1638, when he decided to shift his capital from Agra to Delhi.
 
• It was built by the Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan.
 
 
 
• **Jama Masjid (Delhi)**:
 
 
• It was dedicated to his daughter, Jahanara Begum.
 
• Jama Masjid is also known as the 'Friday mosques'.
 
• Jama Masjid is one of the largest mosques in India.
 
• The Jama Masjid is built mainly of red sandstone and marble that stand as a testimony to the magnificent Mughal architecture.
 
• It has a fountain at the centre and is supported by four kiosks in the courtyard.
 
• The interior walls have scriptures in the Persian style praising Shah Jahan and Jahan Ara.
 
• The inlaid panels of work here are quite similar to that of the Taj Mahal and are common to all the monuments and structures built by the Mughals in Agra.
 
• The Tomb of Salim Chisti is a part of the mosque compound.
